reviews.rationale: Sequential Q2-to-Q3 comparison of selected SEC rows shows GAAP net interest income rising on a larger increase in interest income than in interest expense, while the credit loss provision rose by a similar magnitude, leaving net interest income after provision essentially unchanged. The pretax and net income improvement is therefore attributable in the selected rows mainly to higher noninterest income with noninterest expense roughly flat, not to core spread expansion. The non-GAAP FTE net interest margin moved only marginally, and the FTE net interest income change differs from the GAAP change, so basis differences must be kept separate. Provision growth is material counterevidence to a benign credit narrative and is not explained by these rows. No segment, rate, deposit, mix, reserve, charge-off, capital, guidance or year-over-year evidence is present in this extract, and absence from the extract is not evidence of absence from the filing. Research state held for review pending fuller filing evidence.
